$comment: 🌉️ The mesh-wire republications a producer emits between two settled previews. Each one parses, none of them yields a single drawable mesh, and none of them changes the camera — which is exactly the shape `publish_world3d_scene_bridge_snapshot` used to answer `World3dSnapshotFault::Capacity` for, quarantining the surface for good. Held against the settled payload in `🌉️scene-bridge/🔣️.json`, which every case is applied AFTER.

provenance.reading: [DEBUG] world3d surface=generation3d-generate-preview … meshes=169b instances=267b … against meshes=3644b/4646b/4786b for every settled sample, followed by `world3d bridge fault … fault=Some(Capacity) state-meshes=3` and `frame fault recorded: world3d scene mesh-wire bridge faulted`
provenance.gesture: Add Generation, then 20 world3d gestures interleaved with 3 Form slider drags (updateGenerationValues); the fault fired on the third

cases.name: meshes-without-triangles
cases.why: The measured shape: the producer names its meshes before it has tessellated them, so every record carries no positions and no indices. The parse phase's own `vertex_count() > 0 && indices.len() >= 3` retain drops them all, and the instance retain then drops every instance that referenced them.

cases.name: a-degenerate-mesh-with-too-few-indices
cases.why: Two indices is not a triangle. The retain is a geometry predicate, not an emptiness one, so a non-empty record can still leave the build with nothing to draw.

cases.name: instances-referencing-a-mesh-the-payload-does-not-carry
cases.why: A republication whose instance lane is ahead of its mesh lane. Every instance is dropped by the parse phase's own `meshes.any(id == mesh_id)` retain, so there is no mesh with an instance and therefore no page.

cases.name: an-empty-wire
cases.why: Both lanes empty. This is the case the very first build of a surface survives by accident — its camera digest is new, so it always has a camera page — and every later one did not.
